interpretation.diagram_classification: cosmological / natural-philosophical diagram (concentric scheme of correspondences between macrocosm, time and the human body: elements, seasons, qualities and humours)
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram is a medieval scheme of correspondences linking the world (mundus), the year (annus) and the human being (homo), the macrocosm-microcosm triad written in the central circle. Around this centre, interlaced concentric bands carry the four elements (Ignis, Aer, Aqua, and presumably Terra, which I could not read in Step 1), the four seasons (Aestas, Ver, Autumnus, Hiemps), the four elementary qualities (Calidus, Siccus/Sicca, Frigida, Humidus) and the four humours (Colera, Sanguis, Melancolia, Flegma). Each position joins an element with a season, a quality and a humour. At the top, Ignis, Aestas, Calidus, Sicca and Colera form the fire / summer / hot-dry / choler group. On the right, Aer, Ver, Calidus, Humidus and Sanguis form the air / spring / hot-moist / blood group. At the bottom, Aqua, Hiemps, Frigida, Humidus and a humour label form the water / winter / cold-moist group. On the left, Frigida, Sicca, Autumnus, Melancolia and a label for earth form the cold-dry group. The interlacing bands show that the qualities are shared between neighbouring elements, seasons and humours, so the whole forms a single cyclical system of harmony between cosmos, time and the human body.
interpretation.evidence: The central text "MVNDVS. ANNVS. HOMO." and the labels Ignis, Aqua, Colera, Sanguis, Melancolia, Ver, Aer, Calidus, Sicca, Frigida and Humidus match the standard fourfold scheme of elements, seasons, qualities and humours. Several Step 1 readings are uncertain and should be treated with caution. "Au tum [illegible]" (entry 14) probably reads Autumnus. "Es tas" (entry 5) is probably Aestas. The bottom label "Hi emf" (entry 18) probably reads Hiems. The illegible bottom label (entry 17) may be a humour such as Flegma. A left-hand label and a possible Terra label are not clearly recorded in Step 1. Step 1 also used 'inside outer circle' for almost every label, which gives little structural information. The exact assignment of qualities to each element is partly inferred from the standard scheme, because some of the labels are hard to read. The interlaced bands themselves give visual support for the idea of interconnection and cyclic order.
